newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland, Belgium to cooperate against crime.
newsitem.headline: Poland, Belgium to cooperate against crime.

text.p: Poland, which is seeking to join the European Union, told Belgian Interior Minister Johan Vande Lanotte on Saturday it would work to ensure its eastern borders were well-policed, PAP news agency reported.
Vande Lanotte signed an agreement on cooperation in fighting organised crime, terrorism, extortion, prostitution and trade in people, drugs, forgery, car theft and other international offences.
Polish cabinet chief of staff Leszek Miller said, after talks with the visitor, that Poland had been assured that EU countries would help it protect its borders.

"I stressed strongly that Poland's eastern border will also be the EU's eastern border and therefore efforts must be strengthened to ensure it is safe and watertight," the agency quoted Miller as saying.
EU states are concerned that crime gangs from former Soviet states are operating in Europe and that when Poland joins the bloc, it might be easier for them to enter and operate.
Poland borders Ukraine, Belarus and Russia's Kaliningrad.
Under the agreement signed on Friday, Poland and Belgium will send police liaison officers to their embassy in the other's capital. Miller said this would happen within months.
The Polish officer in Brussels will also be responsible for contacts with the Netherlands and Luxembourg, with which Warsaw already has similar agreements, as it does with France.
